io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: AI agent for SAP analytics and AI consultants. Curated, source-backed intelligence on the SAP analytics services market (Datasphere, Business Data Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, BW/4HANA, Databricks), exposed read-only so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. TEN tools over the PUBLIC tranche: a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, with a full profile per firm; freelance day-rate bands by geography, stack and seniority, where sample_size comes back null when no real observation matches the exact cell and GBP/CHF observations are never folded into the euro band; a live contract radar of publicly promoted SAP analytics openings, each row carrying the original per-job permalink; 4,491 curated market news items, each with the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of 38 study editions (19 deep-research studies, each published in EN and FR) on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics. Counting rows gives 38, counting studies gives 19; the tool returns editions. Free, unauthenticated, read-only: every tool is annotated readOnlyHint and none writes. Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url pointing at the specific analyticslegends.ai page for the record served. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED here, and this is a boundary rather than a gap: the SAP end-customer estate corpus, firm intelligence detail, study bodies and the opportunity-to-consultant matchers are paid tiers; people are never served at all — consultants are held as initials only and no tool returns a person's identity or contact details. SAP's own product documentation is not ours to restate: cite SAP.

server.title: Analytics Legends — SAP Analytics Intelligence

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.endpoint_probe: POST tools/list on https://analyticslegends.ai/mcp -> 200, 20 tools, protocol 2025-11-25, 3 resources, 4 prompts. Paid conformance 2026-08-18 on the deployed fingerprint: 686 assertions, 0 failed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: Curated, source-backed intelligence on the SAP analytics services market (Datasphere, Business Data Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, BW/4HANA, Databricks), read-only, so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. TWENTY tools: FOURTEEN public and unauthenticated, plus SIX a subscriber key opens (listed, refusing by name, never hidden): a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, a profile per firm, and an aggregate count for an agent that needs a number, not a page of rows; a published day-rate aggregate by geography, stack and seniority — small, all secondary sources, sample_size null where no observation matches the cell, GBP/CHF never folded into euro rows; a live contract radar of publicly published SAP analytics openings, each with its own page — filter it by employment_type, because it is mostly PERMANENT roles and an unfiltered page answers a contracting question with salaried jobs; many rows carry a panel-inferred P25-P75 day-rate band for their seniority x product x region cell, served with its basis, sample and source so it is never quotable as the employer's own offer; what is gated there is a FIELD, not a row: the verified link to the original listing is the Consultant deliverable, every other fact and the page stay public; a curated market-news corpus de-duplicated by upstream URL, its size read at query time and returned as _meta.match_count, each item carrying the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of the deep-research studies on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics — each exists in EN and FR, so the tool returns EDITIONS and counting rows double-counts studies. Also public: the CV/profile platforms a consultant can sign up on, the Academy catalogue, and a traversal of the learning knowledge graph. Every tool is annotated readOnlyHint. The fourteen public tools need no credential; the six paid ones need an analyticslegends.ai subscription (Consultant or above) or the MCP Pass (€39.90/month, analyticslegends.ai/pricing) — three open at Consultant (the full concept card, a study body, an Academy module) and three at Legend (firm intelligence, and the SAP end-customer corpus with its per-customer profile). A key on a FREE account gets a small daily taste of the paid tranche (the number is in analytics-legends://tranche). Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED at any tier: the opportunity-to-consultant matchers, and people — consultants are held as initials only; no tool returns anyone's identity or contact details.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.monitoring: Handshake, a real tools/call with data, and latency. Two watchers: a 20-minute tick on the maintainer's workstation (only while awake), and a cloud backstop twice a day calling tools/list AND a data-returning tools/call (added 2026-08-18; before that it watched the website only). Health: https://analyticslegends.ai/api/mcp-health.json — read its generated_at, do not assume a cadence.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.repository_scope: This repository is the server's PUBLIC FACE — manifest, descriptor, client config, docs. It carries no server code (the application repository is private: paid corpus, personal data). tools/list against the endpoint is the authority for the surface.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.tools_served: 20 on this endpoint: 14 public and unauthenticated, 6 gated by tier and refused by name (3 at Consultant, 3 at Legend). The MCP Pass opens all six.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.transport_path: Cloudflare Worker on analyticslegends.ai/mcp* -> Supabase Edge Function -> Postgres
